_note: Example answers used by scripts/demo_plant_health.py. They stand in for what an owner would say; edit them freely. They are the owner's decisions, not research findings.
idea: I want to build an app that helps people determine whether their plants are healthy using their smartphone camera.
title: Plant-health photo app

answers.intent: Yes, that's right. To be precise: it should point out visible symptoms and possible causes, not give a definitive diagnosis.
answers.subject_scope: Start with tomato plants grown by home gardeners and small market gardens; leaves only for the first version.
answers.users: Home gardeners and smallholders who notice spots or discoloured leaves and want a quick first opinion before buying treatments or asking an expert.
answers.classes: Healthy leaf, early blight, late blight, septoria leaf spot, leaf mould, bacterial spot. Anything else must come back as 'not recognised' rather than a forced guess.
answers.dataset: No proprietary images yet. We can collect about 1,500 field photos from partner gardens over two months; an agronomist will review labels on a 10% sample.
answers.inference: On-device inference so it works offline in the field; an optional cloud model later.
answers.model: Fine-tuning a small pretrained image model is acceptable if its licence allows commercial use and it stays under about 20 MB.
answers.capture: Mid-range Android phones from the last four years. Guide the user to photograph one leaf, in daylight, filling most of the frame.
answers.uncertainty: Below the confidence threshold, say 'can't tell from this photo', ask for another photo, and suggest contacting an agricultural extension officer.
answers.privacy: Photos stay on the phone by default. Sharing photos to improve the model is opt-in, with location removed.
answers.backend: No accounts in the first version. A small backend only for opt-in photo uploads.
answers.validation: Hold out photos from gardens not used for training, report per-class precision and recall, and have the agronomist review all errors on the most harmful classes.
answers.success: At least 80% of test users say the guidance helped them decide what to do next, and per-class recall above 0.8 on held-out field photos.
answers.cost_connectivity: It must work offline in the garden. Server costs should stay under about 50 euros per month for the first year.
